text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Figures from the Federal Airport Authority of Nigeria show decline in air passenger traffic; 19 airports handled 1,179,471 passengers in the second quarter of 1996 against 1,232,515 for the corresponding period last year.
- Nigeria's military government may have shelved plans to merge its three distressed merchant banks as serious debt recovery efforts were being made by the banks.
- Traditional ruler bans members of the opposition National Democractic Coalition (NADECO) from holding meetings in southwestern town of Owo.
- Banking sector regulator Central Bank plans decree which will give it powers for outright liquidation of the country's distressed banks from next year, spokesman Tony Ede says.
- Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), which groups all practising doctors, starts a programme of free medical consultations for the elderly in Lagos.
- Fundamentalists criticise Nigerian Moslem leader Muhammadu Maccido, the Sultan of Sokoto, for attending the burial ceremony of the late former Nigerian president Nnamdi Azikiwe.
- Petrol shortages cripple business activities in the southeastern oil city of Port Harcourt.
